utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber would like to inform the parties that pursuant to Rule 15 bis (a), today's hearing will take place in the absence of Judge Kinis. Judge Kinis is away for urgent personal reasons, and Judge Gwaunza and I have conclude that it is in the interests of justice to continue the trial without Judge Kinis, who will be present again on Friday. Mr. Misetic, are you ready to continue your cross-examination? Then, Mr. Theunens, I would like to again remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, first let me go back to a point I made before we paused for the second break yesterday. I had invited to you look through your documents to see if in your report you had made reference to notice to General Gotovina of murders committed by HV. Could you please point me to those.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the second part of the report at the English page 326, I have included a report by the commander of the 3rd Company of the 72nd Military Police Battalion, which is part of 65 ter 419. More specifically the information I have included can be found on -- in the English translations, pages 7 and 8 of 9 of 65 ter 419. And the commander of the 3rd Military Police Company in his report to Major Juric states: "During the searches, i.e., this is upon the arrival of the HV Split Military District units, more specifically the 134th and the 7th Home Guard Regiments in Benkovac on the 5th and the taking control over Benkovac as a whole on the 6th. So during the searches we found five, six dead people, and then we informed the security services." I now skip a part just to speed matters up, or I could read it out entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "During the searches we found five, six dead people, and then we informed the security services, as well as the services in charge of the clearing up of the terrain. Considering the shortness of time passed since our entrance to the city, we assumed that these were people of Croatian ethnicity who have been killed by Chetniks." The reason, Your Honours, I used this information in response to Mr. Misetic's question is that, as I have pointed out earlier, the military police reporting is not the only source of reporting for the operational commander. In this particular case the commander of the Split Military District will receive reports from the commanders -- from the commander of OG Zadar, whereby the commander of OG Zadar will have received reports from his subordinate units who were in Benkovac, namely the 134th and the 7th Home Guard Regiment, in addition, there is the reporting from the department for political affairs, which goes through the chain of command, i.e., from OG Zadar to the Split Military District, and I mentioned this just to explain that the commander has several sources of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if I may stop you for a second there. Do you say that this was reported through these chains, this incident; or do you say, Here we see a report and one could expect, although it could not be established, that that's what happened, that it should be reported?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, indeed it should be reported. But again I wanted to draw your attention to HV doctrine, where it is stated that the commander has to be familiar with this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that Mr. Misetic was seeking your assistance in finding documents in which we find such reports. And that's, I think, what he asked to you do, and I think he will appreciate that you have done it. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. If could I just clarify this now, Mr. Theunens. First, you will agree with me that this report that you're referencing is not a report that goes to General Gotovina. It's a report from the -- Mr. Gransavic [phoen] of the military police to Mr. Juric, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as this specific report is concerned, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you have no evidence at all that this report was copied to the Split Military District, sent to the Military District. I'm not asking you now what you think the theory should have called for. I'm saying you have no evidence that this was send to the Split Military District Command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I would just like add one other document that is 65 ter 4600, where the commander of the 134th Home Guard Regiment reports to his commander, and I draw the conclusion that his commander is General Gotovina. This is a report from the 23rd of August, and it covers the situation in Benkovac and the problems that occurred in Benkovac upon the 134th and the 7th Home Guard Regiments taking over control, whereby commander of the 134th also refers to the presence of a member of the Split Military District Command, i.e., Colonel Sundov, who is the assistant commander for Home Guard, in Benkovac at the time of the arrival of the Split Military District unit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So again my question is, the answer is no, you don't have evidence that General Gotovina was given notice of murders having been committed by someone in the HV?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't come across documents during my -- the preparation of my reports that indicate notice of murders. But again I tried to explain how militaries operate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just while we're on this topic, when you were doing your searches of the OTP's database, did you use word combinations such as "Gotovina," "murder"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I don't remember doing such a specific search. As I explained earlier, I did searches "Gotovina" and "95," "Gotovina" and "94" and other combinations but not specifically directed at murders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. We will let's take that -- Gotovina and 95 is the broadest possible search you could do in the database. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the broadest would be Gotovina "tout court."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Agreed. In terms what we're interested in this for this case for the year 1995 and notice of murders, if you do a search and pull every document that is -- has "Gotovina" and "1995," presumably - correct me if I'm wrong - if there is an document referencing General Gotovina having been put on notice of murders in 1995, that document would presumably come up in your search?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such a specific document would have come up in my search. And as I mentioned, I have not come across such a specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Now, if we could go back to where we left off yesterday. Let me pull up P881.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you would, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now I believe this is the order that you were referencing yesterday which you indicated that you believe General Lausic had - and I don't want to put words in your mouth but - something to the effect of overstepped his authority under Article 8, and I think is the specific document that you refer to, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And if you allow me, Yesterday I had no clear recollection of the document. Now I mean I looked at the document again yesterday afternoon. And when I see the contents of the document, and in particular paragraph 7, which is -- which is visible on the second page, I would like to retract what I said in connection to my initial comment yesterday, that I considered that this order was an example of General Lausic's overstepping his authority. Based again on -- on the contents of this order, and in particular because he orders to establish military police stations all over the territories that have been recaptured, I consider that it is in line with Article 8 of the 1994 rules as well as the document D35 that was discussed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to a different document then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if could I have Exhibit D845 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is a document. It's a report sent from the commander of the 4th Company of the 72nd Military Police Battalion, sent to Major Budimir, on the 7th of August, reporting on his oral order received from General Lausic. And if you look at it, on the 7th of August he says: "Pursuant to the oral order of the chief of the military police administration, Major-General Mate Lausic, received ..." Are you following this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "Received 7 August 1995 at 1310 hours who ordered that a security system be established urgently at the entries and exits of the following warehouses ..." And General Lausic orders three specific warehouses notice Knin area and the wider Knin area, Krka, Senjak and the Golubic depots.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now it goes on to stay: "When the security system is established, the aforementioned senior officers are obliged to write a written report and send it urgently to the MP administration indicating that the security system has been established. The addressee of the report should be Major-General Mate Lausic. Now on the 7th of August, General Lausic is issuing specific orders on specific warehouses that need to be secured with MP personnel. Is this order issued by General Lausic consistent with his powers under Article 8?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you consider this document in isolation, then the initial reaction would be that it goes beyond what is stipulated in the Article 8 because of its specificity. As I tried to explain also during my examination, analysis or intelligent analysis is about looking at individual documents but also putting them in content, and yesterday afternoon I reviewed my report again, and I made a list of the documents that relate to activities including reports an orders of the 72nd Military Police Battalion, both prior to and during Storm, and these documents indicated that indeed there are instructions by Lausic, some of them like this one appear to be more specific than what one would expect from Article 8 of P880, or from D35, but taking context of all the other documents included in my report, I do not see a reason to review my conclusions that Articles 8 and 9 are abided by during Operation Storm, and actually they are also confirmed by D35.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You and I are going to go through the context of all of these orders in a few minutes, but for right now I would like your specific answer. You correct me if I'm wrong, but I understand your answer to be taking this specific order, individually you would consider this order individually to be outside the scope of General Lausic's powers under Article 8. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And there may be reasons for that, but I did not find, or I have not come across information which indicate which reasons General Lausic had for this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have Exhibit D795 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is a document again dated 7 August 1995. It's issued by General Lausic. It's sent to the forward command post Ugljan sent to Major Juric on behalf of the 72nd MP Battalion and sent to the 67th Military Police Battalion Sisak. And in the introduction Mr. Lausic calls upon his own pursuant under Article 8 and issues an order --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there's a problem with the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, sorry. You see there on the 7th of August he sends this order to the three address, and in the introductions he invokes his powers under Article 8. And then again they are to establish the location of every warehouse facility within the entire liberated territory, evaluate a method of physically securing all warehouse facilities, and establishing physical security. They are to enter the warehouse facilities, and issuing mechanical technical devices is not permitted without written clearance from General Zagorac. They are to immediately establish physical security and maintain it until the hand over. And if we turn the page. Paragraph 5 is, they are to submit reports on the implementation of this order starting on the 7th of August and if need be orally to the military police administration. Now here again General Lausic is issuing an even broader order concerning all warehouse facilities on the liberated territory, how they are to do it, and they are to go and secure them. Do you consider that order to be outside the scope of General Lausic's powers under Article 8?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, and for the following reasons: First of all, General Lausic acts upon an instruction from the minister of defence. And also for the second reason is because the Croatian armed force have an interest in having a uniform approach to -- or in dealing with former enemy warehouses, and at that stage, the 7th of August, the military police seemed to be the best suited force to take care of these warehouses to secure them and to prevent people who are not authorised from entering, and so on and so on. And again, as you said yourself, the order explains how they should do it. For me that is in line with Article 8 of the 1994 MP rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let's follow up on that. In addition to having a uniform approach to dealing with warehouses, you would agree with me that it was in the interests of the Croatian armed forces and the Croatian government to have a uniform approach to establishing and re-establishing security in the liberated territory, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You would want a uniform approach in the entire liberated territories on how the security plan is going to be implemented, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question because I have seen the security plan for the Split Military District, i.e., we discuss the one for OG North which was approved by General Gotovina. I have not been able to review the security plans, i.e., the plans that are included in the order for attack Kozjak for the other Military Districts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, if there was a plan worked out between the MUP and the military police administration on how security was going to function, you would agree with me that that plan -- it was in the interests of the Croatian government that that plan be implemented in a uniform approach on the liberated territory, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But I mean at the end we will state, Well, everything was ordered by the chief of the Main Staff because you wanted to have a uniform approach in all of the Military Districts in relation to how to restore Croatian control over the Serb-held areas, and obviously that was not the case. So there are -- there are limits, but this is a very good example. This particular order we're looking at of a specific matter which falls within the professional capabilities of the military police or within the professional tasks of the military police, and where, at a stage when Operation Storm is not yet finished, i.e., with the 7th of August, so the combat units are still needed to conduct military operations, it is -- makes sense to have the military police secure warehouses, and therefore to have a uniform approach in all of the recaptured areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let explore this topic, and let's start from the beginning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I please have Exhibit D409.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think you have seen the document we're putting up right now. These are General Lausic's notes from a meeting that was held on the 2nd of August, 1995 at 10.00 a.m. You are familiar with this, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and I have mentioned them in part 2 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you see all the military people that are present at this meeting. This includes basically every service, every Military District Commander, the minister of defence, Mr. Lausic himself, Mr. Lausic's assistants, like Marijan Biskic Muharem; the chief of the SIS is present, Mr. Gugic at line 7; and intelligence services are present. And if we turn to page 3 of the document, the note where minister Susak begins to speak. The third entry under Minster Susak is "military police must be more energetic in its actions and must prevent all offences." The next entry is "the Military District Commanders must be the ones to pass on to the other commanders the prohibition of any kind of uncontrolled conduct: Torching, looting, et cetera." Next entry is "we must prevent having to take the heros of the homeland war to court. And then PD, political affairs workers, must carry out their tasks of appropriately briefing HV members." And the last line is "the west has given a partial blessing, but nothing must happen to UNPROFOR." Now, and just as a side note, General Gotovina speaks after that, in the fourth entry is "populated areas are included in the defence system." But I want to get what Mr. Susak said. He is talking there about a combination of different measures that need to be taken. Would you agree with me? He says the Military District Commanders need to pass on orders that illegal unlawful conduct, such as torching and looting is banned, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, and just I mean for the people maybe in a non-military mind, passing on does not mean just push forward on an e-mail and say, Well, look here's the order. It means that throughout the chain of command, the orders have to be issued and also their implementation has to be verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think we're all familiar with that, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, let's get to the first line, which is "it is the military police that must be energetic in its actions and must prevent all offences." That is the role of the military police according to Minister Susak on the 2nd, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, but again when we take the 1992 Code Of Military Discipline, as well as regulations that define the tasks of commanders, enforcing discipline is first and foremost a task the commander, and it is only when he fails or is not able to enforce discipline or when there are serious violations that the military police is called upon to intervene and to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is not correct, is it, Mr. Theunens? You read the military police administration's regulations. Have you read them thoroughly?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read them, but I have also read the 1993 Law of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Have you read the 1994 military police administration regulations on what the tasks of the military police are?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. But the military police does not act in isolation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Theunens, no one acts in isolation in the military, do they?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but have I the impression that you try to depict the role of the military police as like a civilian police force. Obviously if in civilian life there is a problem between people, then you call the police to solve it. In the military it is first through the chain of command, whereby the responsibility of the commanders at all command levels is involved, to maintain discipline that's a basic principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We agree on that, Mr. Theunens. You are going to be together for the next two days, so your answers will be much shorter if instead of answering my questions trying to think through what I'm trying to depict, what I'm trying to get at, et cetera, if you just answer and stick to the basic question that I'm asking you and give me the basic answer without the extra spin to try to defeat whatever you think I'm trying to prove, we'll get through this a lot quicker. Okay. Now, Mr. Susak on the 2nd said "military police must be more energetic in its actions and must prevent all offences, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the text says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's get to the part where it says "political affairs workers must carry out their task of appropriately briefing HV members." That might be as clear to the Trial Chamber as to what is referenced by that. You having read the Military District orders to the political affairs workers, what does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the aspects which is, I believe, important in this context is that the assistant commander for political affairs as well as through the political affairs chain have to brief the military personnel about the importance of abiding by the laws of armed conflict also about -- they brief them on morale issues, i.e., keep motivation high and explain them why the upcoming operation important, and again as I pointed out why they have to abide by rules, regulations, including the international laws of war. And laws of armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could turn to page 5 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We saw Mr. Lausic's notes on the 2nd at 10.00, and now we're turning to page 5 of his notes which references the meeting -- I don't think we're on the right page in the Croatian version. I think it's the page prior in the Croatian. Actually it starts on the page prior. It is a meeting at 1730 hours, meeting in the minister's office, according to Mr. Lausic. The persons present at this meeting on the 2nd at 5.30 p.m. are Minister Susak, Minister Jarnjak, MUP assistant Minister Josko Moric, and obviously Mr. Lausic himself. Now they're discussing at the meeting at 5.30 the agreement on two issues: On the check-points in the combat zone combat operations zones on possible refugees, Minister Jarnjak makes comments, "it cannot be the same model as Operation Flash as more places will be occupied. The military police follow the front line and the civilian police enter populated areas." If we turn the page, the rest of the discussion about which highways are going to be closed down, military police must announce passage of military convoys, et cetera, et cetera. So let's establish first of all there's a meeting between those four individuals meaning two ministers and their top assistant ministers on police issues at 5.30 on the 2nd of August, and now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have -- just a moment please. Exhibit D794, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In Exhibit D794 you see that the next day, after the meeting at the top level, there's a working meeting held between the heads of the Ministry of the Interior, as well as the heads of the military police administration, and the SIS administration, on the 3rd of August. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And it says it's a working meeting of the top officials held in the MUP, devoted to coordinating the actions of the MUP, military police and SIS in preparation of and during the planned offensive activities of the HV in the coming herd. "The meeting began at 1300 hours and the following persons were present." If you look through you see who was present from the MUP, who was present from the military police administration and SIS. You will not that only is General Gotovina not present, but no one from the military chain of command is present at this time meeting. Do you agree with that? When I say "military chain of command," I mean from the Main Staff down that line.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You -- I have seen this document. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, but I'm not 100 percent sure, and I have to cope with the technical limitations that when have you a military document it is nice to be able to flip through it and see who signed which is most of the times indicated at the end and just to scan it, but I mean I accept technical limitations. What I try to do is review the documents after my cross-examination because I have the privilege of having access to them via e-court in my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if you look through this when you get a chance, you see that they discuss the details at the working meeting of all the technical aspects of working out security traffic, those types of issues that you would have in restoring security to a liberated area, okay? Now, I ask you and I'm going to back now, but I wanted to point that out to you that there's a follow-up meeting on the 3rd after the meeting of the two ministers and their police assistants on the 2nd. There's a working meeting held to implement the details of their agreement. If you look at page 3 of this document, and this will be -- I just want you to note it because I'm going to go back and discuss this. Page 3 in the English and the section where Major-General Mate Lausic is speaking he says in the second bullet point, he talks about the main negative experiences in Operation Flash were the following ... And then the last sentence of the second bullet appointed is: "He also emphasised that he now authorised UVP and military police administration officers to replace the commanders of VP units on the spot should they notice any irregularities in their work." Does that indicate to you that these UVP officer have the power -- do you agree that they have the power to replace, for example, battalion -- military police battalion commanders on the spot if there are any irregularities in their work?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is, in my view, in line with the doctrine, because we are talking about specialized units with specialized personal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's go to, Mr. Registrar, to Exhibit D267, please. And if we could go to page 4 in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is the order, just so yo usee it. It is the 2nd August order issued by General Lausic to all of the subordinated military police battalions and other military police assets regarding -- we'll get the subject line, preparations of military police units to perform military police tasks in the areas of responsibility of the Croatian army Military Districts during upcoming operations. And if we read page 10, second paragraph -- I'm paragraph 10, I apologise, second paragraph: "I appoint major Ivan Juric in a group of officers from the regular VP section and the VP administration crime section to assist in commanding and organizing the activities of the 72nd VP battalion and 73rd Split VP Battalion, that shall perform tasks in its own area of responsibility and provide necessary civilian to the 72th VP battalion. The commanders of the 72nd VP battalion and 73rd VP battalion shall be subordinated to Major Ivan Juric." Now, if we go to the next page in the English, the first bullet point, he says what the reporting requirements are, and he says: "The commanders of the 72nd VP Battalion and the 73rd VP Battalion shall report to major Ivan Juric, who shall report to the VP administration until 2000 hours every day starting from 4 August 1995." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So the 72nd Military Police Battalion commander, Major Budimir, is to report to Major Juric, Major Juric is then to file a report with General Lausic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. But in this order, I -- because I discuss it on English page 208 of part 2 of the report, Lausic also confirms the subordination of the military police within the daily operational chain of command to the operational commanders. So again it is confirmations of Articles 8 and 9 whereby to facilitate the command and control over 72nd and 73th. General Lausic appoints Major Ivan Juric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's now turn to Exhibit D268, please. While we are flipping to that, do you see and agree with me that when you read the document I just showed you combined with the notes of the meeting on the 3rd with the MUP officials where Mr. Lausic said that these UVP administration officers had the power to replace commanders in the field that Major Juric had the authority from General Lausic to replace Major Budimir if he found that there were irregularities in his work?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I said that was in line with Articles 8 and 9 of the 1994 military police regulations, as well as what is described in Croatian armed forces doctrine as the professional line, whereby a distinction is made between command and control along the professional line on the one hand, and command and control along the direct or operational line on the other hand. And that can be find on English page 130, part 1, of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you a background question, Mr. Theunens. Do you agree that General Lausic could not issue an order to General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not directly. However, I have seen an example and that is on the 9th of August, in his overview report on the activity of the military police, General Lausic includes a sentence where he says, I please request that the military police units be relieved of combat tasks and can return or can turn to regular military police tasks. This report by Lausic covers all military police units throughout Croatia. Now, his report is sent to Mr. Susak, General Cervenko, and if I remember well also the Military District Commanders. And the day after he issues an order to the effect that military police units should be relieved from combat tasks and should carry out regular military police tasks, this order is based on an instruction of Mr. Susak, and it is send to the Military District Commanders, all of them. Subsequently to this order by Lausic, General Gotovina issues an order to his Operational Group commanders, to implement Lausic's order, i.e., to relieve the military police units of combat tasks and allow them to carry out regular military police tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I think we need to clarify some of your answers there.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And if you allow, I can just give you the references.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to put it on the screen right now, okay.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And we'll go back to the document that is on the screen now. But while you've gone off on this topic now, let's cover it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: D837, Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is -- oh, sorry. This is an order, it's not issued to General Gotovina, as you said. It's issued to the military police battalions about removing the combat units, right? If you scroll down in the English?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But could can we see the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'll show you the end. Hold on.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "With the aim of deploying the anti-sabotage units of the military police ... in order to search, mop up the liberated territory of the Republic of Croatia. I hereby ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "... order all military police units engaged in combat activities are to be disengaged from the areas of combat activities at 0700 hours on the 10th of August." And then talks about anti-tank battalions, et cetera being given. If we go down to see "the delivery submitted to," and then the last line is: "To the attention of." If we could go to the Croatian version, please, signature line. Meaning: For information. Right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And that is what I meant to say, and this is a referred to in part 2 of my report, English page 226.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, this is an important distinction though, because we got off on this topic now because you wanted to such that General Lausic to indirectly issue an order to General Gotovina which is not what this document is doing.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What this document is doing is issuing an order to a unit that is part of the units of General Gotovina, i.e., the military police unit of General Gotovina, and that's why it is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, this is sort of -- if I may use the expression putting the cart before the horse, because you have already concluded that General Gotovina's units, and therefore you're interpretations flow from that. My -- my specific remember, this is a document that you and I talked about yesterday. When I talked about what would happen now, you have seen the order by General Lausic. It is given to General Gotovina for information. Ten minutes after General Gotovina receives this order, he issues another order to Mr. Budimir that says, You are not to withdraw the anti-terrorist platoons. You are to ignore the order by General Lausic, and you are to continue doing the tasks that you have been doing until now. I believe your answer to me was in that situation, General Gotovina's order would prevail, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would first like to address your comment where you state that the 72nd Military Police Battalion is not a unit of the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I didn't say that. Where did I say that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You state in page 21, line 9, "if I may use the expression putting the cart before the horse, because you have already concluded that General Gotovina's units, and therefore your interpretation flows from that," I understood that in the sense that you -- in your view the 72nd Military Police Battalion is not a unit of General Gotovina, whereas based on my analysis and, for example, 65 ter 5768 is a table of manpower which mentions the 72nd Military Police Battalion among the units of the Split Military District. This is one prior to Operation Storm. There are similar tables during Operation Storm. 10th of August we have 65 ter 4584 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens. Yes but I'm -- you're citing a bunch the documents that we're going to have to enter into evidence. Your string-citing documents and they are not in answer to my question, because you misunderstood what I said in the first place. So if we could hold off on the tangential issues that you find in my questions, and let's focus again in on what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the key issue is to who does the 72nd Military Police Battalion belong.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And that's why I asked you the question quite specifically at the end, which was it's your position -- it's your position that had General Gotovina issued an order saying, Ignore this order by General Lausic. Your position is because you believe this unit is a unit of the Split Military District, that General Gotovina's order prevails. I'm just trying to establish your position. I'm not so much worried that you can try and figure out my position.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But yesterday you were asking a hypothetical question, and I stated well, I give a hypothetical answer to a hypothetical question. Referring to this -- to the document -- I mean the order by Lausic which is sent for information to the Military District Commanders, there is a response by Gotovina in a sense that he forwards the order to his military police units, whereby he basically confirms what General Lausic orders. And that is 65 ter 884, page 226 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. How does that answer my question?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean I'm confused by the hypothetical question. So I'm trying to give you a concrete question -- a concrete answer to a concrete document. I mean, the concrete document being the document -- the order by General Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to use a concrete example to try to figure out what your understanding is of the interrelationship between General Lausic's role with the military police and General Gotovina's role, which your further answer and further cites the 65 ters doesn't help me. So let's focus in on it, and say my hypothetical now is: Based on this document that General Gotovina one hour later issued an order saying, Ignore this order by General Lausic, your position is General Gotovina's subsequent order prevails?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my position in relation to a hypothetical question. Now we have a concrete situation, and I cannot deny a concrete document. And, in my view, the answer to a concrete question whereby I can see documents and draw conclusions from these documents is more relevant than speculating about hypothetical questions and hypothetical answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, part -- if I may say that part of what I believe the role of the expert witness is is to help the Trial Chamber understand the overall picture and the overall relationship between the two. I am using this specific example so that you can assist all of us in the courtroom, if you can, to explain that general relationship which we're all going to having to figure out in this trial. To let me focus in again. In this specific case what happens if General Gotovina issues a counterorder? Is it your position that General Gotovina's order prevails?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Your Honours, my position is that paragraph 5 of D35 would apply, which means that General Lausic's order would prevail theoretically, because I assume that General Gotovina would consult General Cervenko, would consult Mr. Susak, and that on that level agreement would be found, because I will also assume that General Gotovina would have good reasons to say to General Lausic, Look, I can't have my military police do what you order them to do by this order, because this and this reason, and that then, as is done in the military staff and a military environment, there is a dialogue between all people concerned in order to come to a satisfactory solution. This is not a quiz.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But this is it also a military in realtime where seconds and minutes matter. Do you agree with me? In a combat situation you need to know whose order prevails, right? You don't have time to hold a mediation session. You don't have time for consultations. You need to know the hierarchy. That is how the military functions in all militaries; doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, but that is why there is paragraph 5 in D35 to deal with these kind of issues, i.e., when there appears to be a conflict between orders through the operational chain and orders through the professional chain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So the answer is General Lausic wins. I'm not disagreeing with you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't call it that he wins, but based on D35, Lausic's order would reveal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now if we could go back to the document I had on the screen which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just ask a question. I'm just verifying that I understand what this issue is about, which is of a rather technical nature. Article 8, Article 9, they give not very precise, defined command structures. Of course you say Article 8, Article 9 is clearly -- makes a distinction between the two lines of command. Now, what happened yesterday apparently was that you were asked about whose orders would prevail, and you very much resisted to answer that question, which was put to you in a rather abstract nature, and I got the impression at that time, when you said, Give me a document and I'll tell you that you were struggling with under what circumstances exactly Article 8, and on what subjects or circumstances exactly Article 9 would apply. I think you had difficulties in giving an abstract answer on the orders of the one would prevail or the orders of the other would prevail, because I understood your testimony that it depended exactly on what was the content of the order, would it fit in Article 8, would it fit in Article 9? Now, today, apparently, you are given an example, a document, where apparently there is the one claiming that the military police should do what he has ordered, Lausic, and that apparently this is challenged, or there is an competing claim of command on the specific issue of this document. And the one issues an order under Article -- and the other ones gives an order which is under the other Article, so there are two competing claims, apparently in an area where it might not be that easy, or perhaps it is easy, to define exactly whether they are working within the scope of Article 8 or Article 9. Again, apparently the issue is whose orders prevail? And I understand from your answers that, still, that is to be assessed on the basis of the specific order, time, place, all circumstances, whether it is the professional command as you said, or the other -- I think you called it the direct command.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or the operational command, just the same, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for my information, have I understood your testimony correctly because a lot of questions have been put, a lot of answer have been given, a lot of pushing, and a lot of resistance in answering, I noticed, and I just wanted to be sure for myself that I understood your testimony correctly, and if Mr. Misetic would think that I need further details or further matters to know, he will certainly ask you any additional questions. But I just wanted to make a short stop and verify whether I had lost track or not, or not yet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, you have provided correct picture of my answers and of the issue at stake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Misetic, not to say that this is the last. I said I wanted to make a midway stop just to see whether I was on track, totally different from where you and/or Mr. Theunens were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think y ou were, so I'm going to go back into it further.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I asked about this specific order. If we go back to the first page of this document, please I'm sorry, my mistake [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said to see whether I was on track totally different from where you and/or Mr. Theunens were. You said and that's -- you were, so I'm on the wrong track. As far as Mr. Theunens concerned, apparently I'm not, but I'm on the wrong track as far as you are concerned, and I give you all opportunity to further clarify what you think is the right track and which is apparently a different track from what I understood Mr. Theunens track to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I understood Mr. Theunens and I to be on the same page at the end, which now I understand given his answer to your question that he and I are not on the same page anymore, so we're going to go back into it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I could go to the -- the subject is Disengagement Of Combat Units, and the order says at the top: "All military police units engaged in combat activities are to be disengaged from the areas of combat activities at 0700 hours." Combat activities, do you consider that professional activities or operational activities?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat activities are operational activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now your answer when I put this order to you was that under paragraph 5 of D35, your answer to me was General Lausic would prevail. So I'm not confused because this is an order to remove combat units from operational activity issued by General Lausic, right, and you answered that D35, paragraph 5 meant that in the event of a conflict between General Gotovina and General Lausic, General Lausic would reveal. Now in response to the Presiding Judge's questions you have made a distinction between whether the issue dealt with professional activities or operational activities, and so I put it to you, and I'm going put it to you, there is no distinction between professional activities or operational activities in the event of any decision by General Lausic and order with respect military police units, whether they're engaged operationally or whether they are engaged in professional tasks, his orders prevail under paragraph 5 of D35. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we're mixing up things. Because what the Presiding Judge described is my position in relation to the distinction between the professional line and the operational line. And the Presiding Judge also highlighted that it is very difficult or impossible for me to give an answer to an abstract or a hypothetical question, and I would prefer to see the document. Independent of whether this specific document dealt with professional issues or operational issues. Here we a have order by General Lausic which follows, and I think it is important to mention a request he has included in his report to the minister of defence, which is also send to the Military District Commanders the day before, the order here does not show whether there has been any consultation between General Lausic, Mr. Susak, and the Military District Commanders as to well, what do we do with that request of General Lausic, what we see is that a day after his request, he issues this order which indeed it covers operational matters because it's the operational use of military police units who are being used for combat activities, and we see and I have also included that in my report on page 226 that this order is abided by or is implemented by General Gotovina and that he issues an order to his OGs, 65 ter 2316, in order to implement Lausic's order and relieve the military police units of combat tasks, and again it is a very specific situation, and therefore I can answer that question. In other situations the answer may be different, and that'd why, as the Presiding Judge summarized, it is important to look at the specifics and to look at the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. But I want to make sure that we agree -- and this is an example even -- in respect to military police in operational matters General Lausic, at least in this example, under paragraph 5 of D35, his order would prevail over General Gotovina's order.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just now for me to understand, is the specific issue here that he did not issue an order on his own but that there was a higher level communication about what to do under those circumstances? Is that what you here say that the order prevails, or is it on the basis of the structure itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- in my view this order has to be seen notice context of the situation. This order dates from the 9th of August. Certain patterns are visible throughout the areas that have been recaptured by the Croatian forces. And these patterns of activities and of incidents directly affect the role -- sorry, I rephrase it. Fall within the competencies of the military police. Now General Lausic sees that the military police units are mainly used for combat tasks. He based on this order and the request he issued a day before, has a different view on the use of military police in the liberated areas, and considers that the military police should actually be used for military police tasks. Therefore, this order is issued to the military police units in the Military Districts for the Military District Commanders. Now, the fact that General Gotovina on his turn issues an order to his military police -- to his OGs, I apologise, to his OGs, 65 ter 2316, in order to relieve the military police units from combat tasks shows that General Gotovina also plays a role in this chain of command, i.e., in the command over the military police, and there is no -- it's not about an academic interpretation or whether it is Article 8 or 9. I do agree with Mr. Misetic that here in this order we actually deal with matters that should be covered by Article 9, but in any event the order is issued. Now, if you would use this order to generalise the situation -- and state or draw certain conclusions in relation to the role of General Gotovina and/or General Lausic in the area of command and control over the military police, well, there is lots of other documents which are included in my report that actually show that also General Gotovina -- General Gotovina is in a position to issue orders to the military police, and I emphasise that the 72nd Military Police Battalion is a unit of the Split Military District. And I apologise for being so long, but this is not a yes or no, or a black or white situation. There is a lot of grey and I tried to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Theunens, I will get back to you later on there point that you seem to think that this order by General Lausic required another order by General Gotovina. I'll put to that you we'll deal with this issue now that you have raised yet another issue, but can you explain to me why General Lausic sends an order. It is clearly addressed amongst others the 72nd Military Police Battalion VP Split. Are you saying now that that order has no effect unwilling now General Gotovina gets involved on issues his own order, or are you perhaps confusing the fact that General Gotovina issues an act of defence order in which he reports what is is now happening with the anti-terrorist units of the military police? Correct me if I'm wrong, there is no need for a second order by General Gotovina to the 72nd MPs once Mr. Lausic has issued an order, is there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that there is an order from General Gotovina to his OGs in order to relieve the military police from combat tasks, and we would benefit from seeing 65 ter 2316 on the monitor, and then we can see it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to back to you later on because I would like to keep the tempo going, but we will certainly deal with at a later point. But right now, let's go back to D268, please. This is an order from the 2nd of August, reinforcement of the 72nd Military Police Battalion. If we turn to page 2 at the bottom. It says, number one is a group number one is a group of UVP officers led by Major Ivan Juric. It talks about others from the general VP department, Ante Glavan who is from the crime police section of the military police administration. That group is formed, and it says: "Major Ivan Juric's task in the command system, he is superior to the 72nd VP and 73rd VP commanders with regard to the 73rd VP extending assistance to the 72nd VP." And if we could turn the page: "He is responsible for the implementation of all military police tasks in the 72nd VP zone of responsibility." Then the final two points: "He is authorised to undertake all measures to ensure efficient and effective implementation of military police tasks in the 72nd military police and north OS zones of responsibility." And finally: "Reporting shall be pursuant to order of the chief of the UVP ... dated 2 August 1995." And that is the order we have already seen which was D267 saying that at 8.00 p.m. every night Juric is supposed to send a report after having received reports from the 72nd and 73rd. Now if we go to Exhibit D26 --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours there is also a paragraph that you didn't read out where it states that in relation to Juric he shall cooperate and coordinate the implementation of tasks with the workers of civilian police or the police administration Ministry of Interior as well as the Split Military District and the assistant commander for security an information --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is an important point, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I just wanted to -- mention it for the record that this is also included that Juric indeed exercises the authorities as defined by Lausic over the 72nd and 73rd, but he coordinated and cooperates with civilian police, SIS, as well as the operational commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And I thank you actually for bringing that to my attention, because that is relevant to a point that you raised on direct. It doesn't say Juric is subordinated to the Split Military District; it says he shall cooperate and coordinate with the Split Military District, and there is no difference -- distinction made between his cooperation and coordination with the Split Military District and MUP, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but the command and control arrangements for the military police have not changed. And we have seen that D35 confirms the 1994 military police rules, so there is no need to emphasise it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There is an immediate to emphasise it Mr. Theunens because Major Juric is not part of the Split Military District. He is not subordinated to the Split Military District, is he?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... show me the order where Major Juric is subordinated to the commander of the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen no orders indicating that Major Juric is subordinated to the Split Military District, but as I see his role as coordinator, i.e., to facilitate command and control over 72nd and 73rd in the aspect of 73rd providing assistant to the 72nd as is indicated in -- in the order we see now, I don't think that that is of relevance for the command and control over the Split Military District military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I do see it as relevant, and correct me if I'm wrong, but we've now gone through the process where Major Juric -- it says that the commanders of the 72nd and 73rd are subordinated to Major Juric. Major Juric has the power to replace the commanders of the 72nd and 73rd if he finds irregularities in their work. That is more than a coordinator; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we see the first page of this order, or the second page, sorry. So at he bottom we see Juric the task is to shall superior -- excuse me, superior to the 72nd and the 73rd with regard to the 73rd extending assistant to the 72nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes you ignore the next page.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not ignoring it. I'm just trying to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Please take in the next sentence, as you are fond of saying, you take one sentence out of isolation, so let's look at the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He is responsible for the implementation of all military police tasks in the 72nd VP zone of responsibility. Right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But he can be responsible to General Lausic or to General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, have you found any evidence at all to indicate that he either received an order from General Gotovina or issued one report to General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to General Gotovina, but there are documents -- there is at least one document included in my report, and if I remember well, it's 65 ter 419, where we see that Major Juric is in contact with -- he is meeting and coordinating with an Operational Group commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is because he is meeting with MUP, SIS, Split Military District, that is the point you just highlighted in this document, isn't it? That's his job, to coordinate?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there is no references to MUP or SIS in that particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Does it have to be in a particular document for you to know that he is coordinating with the MUP? Do you disagree now that he was coordinating with the MUP while he was there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not what I'm saying, Your Honours. What I'm saying is that in 65 ter 419, we see that Major Juric is in -- call it operational contact with an operational commander and this commander is a subordinate of General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now let's go back to the question that I asked, and if you could again focus. Did you find a report either an order from General Gotovina to Juric, or did you ever find Juric reporting to General Gotovina in written form? Did you find any such documents?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't found or I haven't come across such a document. The closest document, if I can express myself that way, is the operational diary, where a -- an unidentified representative of the military police, sometimes he is identified as the commander of the 72nd Military Police Battalion attends the working meetings of the Split Military District Command and its subordinate commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'm glad you said that because what your answer now reveals to me is that you actually went and looked for such orders to Juric or reporting by Juric to General Gotovina. Right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that I did a specific search for any contact between General Gotovina and Major Juric. What I did is searches on key words, on numbers of orders. I did indeed searches and extensive searches in order to determine how Articles 8 and 9 of the 1994 military police regulations were implemented prior to, during, and after Storm, and these searches would also have revealed any documents indicating contacts between General Gotovina and Major Juric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, you're a military man. You want to assert that Juric was subordinated to General Gotovina. Well --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I haven't said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, so who is he subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Juric is sent by General Lausic to facilitate the command and control -- I mean, I would like to quote the document literally so to -- if we could see the previous page again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm not -- I would think, Mr. Theunens, that it shouldn't be that hard of a question. Mr. Juric is sent into the field, he is a military man. Starting with President Tudjman on down, can he tell me who his next superior officer is?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he is sent by General Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I know who he is sent by. Who is his -- who is he a subordinate of?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you say it should not be that difficult to answer the question. Apparently the witness finds it difficult to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think he does, Judge. I think he knows and just doesn't want to answer, which is my frustration is here because he knows the answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He just said he's not subordinated to General Gotovina, Judge, so who -- who is left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because you say it's a simple question and apparently the witness considers it's a more complex question, and I would invite you to allow him to explain if he disagrees with you on certain matters. Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I confirm that I have not come across documents that indicate that Major Ivan Juric is subordinated to General Gotovina. And therefore, based on this document, I conclude that he is subordinated, at least according to the professional chain, to General Lausic, chief of the military police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is the answer I wanted to get to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, here is the question, and if you need more time we're coming up on a break but I would like an answer to this question. You have seen documents now on the 2nd of August there is a meeting between two ministers, Jarnjak and Susak. Their two top aides for police matters are also present at the meeting. On the 3rd there is a working meeting between MUP and the military police and SIS to implement the agreement reached the day before between the two ministers. Do you agree with me that there is no person in the military chain of command, meaning from the Main Staff on down, that is present at this working meeting to create a plan?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My question is this: From a military perspective, General Lausic does not issue orders to General Gotovina. There is no one present at this meeting who can issue an order to General Gotovina or any Military District Commander. Let's not put this only on General Gotovina because Operation Storm deals with the Split Military District, the Gospic Military District, the Karlovac Military District. We have multiple Military District commanders who take part in Operation Storm. My question for you is this, and if can you help me with the logic of this: Two ministers reach an agreement, their subordinates in the civilian ministries implement a plan, and then this plan is left to be implemented by people, military people, who aren't present at the meetings and who have no obligation to implement this plan, do they, because there is no order from anyone in the military line requiring them to implement anything that is agreed upon at these meetings. Now, I'm just going to put it to you that my position is that General Lausic is the one at the meeting with the power to implement the plan through the military police units. I'd like to know from you, since it's your -- as I understand your position, it is not General Lausic's job on a daily operational level or it's not his job that he can implement the plans for security, that that is left to the zone commanders. How is it from a military perspective that plans can be drawn up and then not given to, for example, General Cervenko to pass an order to all the Military District Commanders that this is how the plan is supposed to function? Why is it left, in your view, to just apparently -- if General Gotovina wants to implement it, he can; if General Norac in Gospic wants to implement it, he can, maybe they can a la carte chose different parts of the plan that they like, that they don't like. Who -- what is the authority that, in your view, required Military District Commanders to implement a plan that was agreed upon between two ministries?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was referring to the security plan, I referred to the security plan of, I believe it was OG Zadar which was 65 ter 171. I'm not sure about which plan you're talking now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me clarify right there. You're talking about the security plans within the Split Military District for Operation Oluja/Kozjak that are done by the 2nd of August; correct? Those orders are issued 1st and 2nd of August; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Subsequent to that, those orders, I have taken you through documents now to show there is another meeting at the ministerial level, a working meeting that takes place, this is what we are going to do, this is how MUP and the military police are going to coordinate their activities, et cetera, et cetera. There's no presence of military, meaning military chain of command, and I don't mean Mr. Lausic here --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- at the meeting, yet you want to suggest that operationally they're subordinated to General Gotovina so presumably your position would be that if that is the plan reached between Jarnjak and Susak and worked out by their subordinates, that that plan had to be implemented by the district commanders, Norac, Basarac, Gotovina, et cetera? My question to you is, how do you jump from essentially what is civilian government plan to restore security, coordinate activities, et cetera, and then just leave it to people who have no legal obligation to implement the plan? Because it hasn't been given to General Cervenko to say we're now going to coordinate with MUP, zone commanders this is what you are supposed to do, this is the agreement between Susak and Jarnjak, I sign off on the agreement as your commander and here is what you are going to do, and here is how you are going to coordinate, and here is where the check-points are going to be set up. I -- okay. Let me hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting you refer to with -- between the ministers of interior and including also Mr. Moric and General Lausic, if I remember the document well, we saw had two major topics, check-points and refugees, and it is logical that at the highest level one agrees about a uniform approach, i.e., in the manner how shall we organise check-points, how will the military police and the civilian police cooperate, how will we organise this. Not only in relation to check-points but also in the treatment of refugees. And then subsequently, there is an agreement about the common approach by the entire territory that is to be recaptured whereby the specific measures, I mean, for example, the specific location of check-points, obviously the military -- the local military police commander will make a proposal to his operational commander as to where they are to be located, but we have discussed documents - and I have included those in my report - that the operational commander, be it General Gotovina or his Chief of Staff Brigadier Ademi, or even OG commanders, can order the military police to organise check-points in particular locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. This is my final question, Your Honour, before the break. Is it not more logical to you, Mr. Theunens, that the agreement was reached between the two ministers, a plan was worked out between General Lausic and his subordinates and Mr. Moric and his subordinates on the 3rd, Mr. Lausic then appoints Mr. Juric from his administration in Zagreb to go out in the field with the authority over the 72nd and 73rd MPs to implement what he had agreed at a meeting on the 2nd and 3rd to do and that that's the chain of command as to how these security measures were to be implemented? Is that also a logical interpretation to you as to how this was supposed to work?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, theoretically it is a logical interpretation, but from the documents we have discussed, and, for example, the earlier request by Mr. Lausic on the 9th of August where he states, please relieve the military police units from combat tasks, that is, for me, one of several indicators. And the other indicators are the documents showing that the operational commanders are issuing orders to the military police in their zone of responsibility, that this logic, the theoretical logic you have described is not implemented in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm going continue on this topic, so I think it might be a good time for a break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It certainly is time for a break. We will resume, five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you may continue, but perhaps I make again a short stop --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to see whether ... Thinking about the evidence and your questions and trying to follow and to understand, it came to my mind at one moment that the command structures, as we find them in 8 and 9, which may create some problems in defining what is exactly in 8 and what is in 9, et cetera, that another element, what is apparently introduced through your questions, is not precisely who is in command on the professional or the operational -- but that there's a higher level, which is availability. Availability to focus on the police tasks, even when performing police tasks, 8 and the would still be in place, so as where to put check-points, what to do, et cetera, at the same time, of course, the professional aspects, for example, uniforms all other kinds of organisational issues. But it seems that the issues about 8 and 9 and how to resolve conflicts there, that there is an another level, that is not who is in command and on what aspects of the performance of tasks but also who decides that rather than to focus on police tasks with all the structures of -- of command and what kind of command, command on what aspects, who is in charge, also will the military police, primarily, be put at the disposal of those who are responsible for combat operations; or will they be, primarily, be at the disposal of those who primarily deal with the performance of what I would say specific police tasks. That is an element which, as I said before, came to my mind, and whether, in terms of command and looking at Article 8 and 9, this question about, could I say availability or primary focus on one task or the other, whether that would is covered by 8 and 9 is a question, and whether that would be resolved in every respect by conflicts, how to -- what the procedure would be if there are conflicts. If we're talking about conflicts, I can imagine conflicts between -- drawing a line between 8 and 9, but I also can imagine that there may be conflicts on that higher level of availability, primary focus on combat tasks, that's some thoughts that came into my mind and which I briefly discussed with Judge Gwaunza and similar thoughts came to her mind, and sometimes it's -- at least the Chamber considers it wise to share with you what comes into our mind that. It is not final conclusions but, rather, an understanding or a provisional understanding or analysis and what thoughts are then developed so that you can address that you know what is on our minds, and that you better are in a position to address the matters that came into our mind. Mr. Misetic, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have to confess I'm not sure what the issue is, but if you allow me, I think I do. First just let me in terms of terminology state that we don't accept - and you'll get that later in cross - Mr. Theunens's creation of professional and operational lines. That doesn't appear in the rules, and he is referring to something from 1992 which was cancelled by the order of Mr. Susak on D35. Although there is a professional line, that has nothing to do with command and control. I think we established, first of all, command and control rests only with the military police administration. And command and control as a military matter, as you are well familiar and you yourself brought it up in this trial, there is an difference between operational command and operational control. That is going to be the issue in this case. With respect to tasks, I think you also need to keep in mind, Your Honour, Article 10 of the regulations, Article 10 spells out what are the, if I can use the term "permanent tasks" of the military police which when a later witness comes, who will be more familiar with it than Mr. Theunens is, and I don't want to reveal his name now. There will be a later witness who will explain to you the difference between the permanent tasks of the military police, and if we -- I can bring up P880, if necessary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I don't think, Mr. Misetic -- I appreciate, of course, that you -- that you respond to this. At the same time, of course, I was not aiming at triggering a further debate on the matter, but I expressed that these thoughts had come into our minds. Again, I emphasise, not conclusions but mere thoughts and an attempt to try to understand the issue. And if you are aware of our thoughts, you also know better what needs to be corrected or what needs to be clarified, and I see that you started already clarifying the issue, but it would be no problem if you do that in the further cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just so that I don't waste any time addressing your issue, if could specifically tell me what issue you would like to have addressed. Are you saying you think it may be who is available to implement these tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who decides on availability for certain tasks?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's go through this and let's talk about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to give an example, if today I say, You're not available for combat tasks anymore, and someone else claims that a person should be available for combat tasks, that is a matter a decision on apparently on availability for different --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When we're talking about combat tasks, I think -- and if I may, it's an in-house witness, so I don't feel as uncomfortable saying it front of him. I think Mr. Theunens was incorrect on that point, but I would like now like to go right into it. P880.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't want to be argumentative, but it's not me who created or invented the professional and the direct line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
