The reports -- it is daily activities or every other day or whatever the frequency of the reports is, what I'm asking you is: Major Juric is dealing with reporting those types of issues, meaning crime processing as I have described it, and setting up these MUP -- military police check-points. Given your answer before the break, doesn't that -- are you -- I would then logically follow you're saying that those tasks fall within the professional line?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we have -- we have to make a distinction between what he is reporting on and who is ordering the issues he is reporting on. There's no doubt that Juric reports to Lausic or to General Lausic about the activities of the military police which cover both professional as well as operational aspects. However, as I mentioned earlier, on the -- these reports, in my view, do not always allow to conclude who ordered to conduct these activities. The reason why I mention this is that that was a second aspect of your initial question. In addition to the instructions given by Lausic and/or Juric, there are also instructions an orders issued by the operational commanders dealing with similar matters, for example, the establishment of check-points. And that's why on the basis of a report, which does not indicate who issued a task, it is difficult to draw a clear conclusion on that aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, without going over the last hour that we've gone through, and I will tell what you my understanding is of your testimony thus far so we don't have to repeat it. Major Juric is under the command of General Lausic. He is not under the command or not subordinated to General Gotovina. He is not receiving orders from General Gotovina. He is not issuing reports to General Gotovina. He is issuing reports to General Lausic. He is completing tasks which he has been charged with from General Lausic. I'm trying -- we see the types of tasks that you acknowledge that he is dealing with are joint check-points with the MUP, crime processing or the work of the crime police of the 72nd MP Battalion. Looking at it from the perspective of what Major Juric is doing -- and you were the one who made this distinction before the break that well, Major Juric is dealing with professional line tasks and General Gotovina is dealing with operational tasks. My question to you is: Now since we have now established that Major Juric is dealing with tasks such as joint MUP check-points and crime processing, given your answer before the break, is my conclusion wrong, that you mean that Major Juric, when he is dealing with joint check-points with MUP and crime processing, is dealing with "professional line tasks"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the transcript from prior to the break, but I remember that you asked me whether the principle of unit of command was violated because of the fact that both Juric and General Gotovina were issuing orders, and I replied that we would have to analyse the specific orders and then to see whether they address tasks that fall under the professional line or whether they concerned tasks that fall under the operational line. Again, Juric reports here on certain activities. I have testified that certainly initially the plan or the instructions given by General Lausic to the military police battalions include the establishment of check-points. Subsequently there is coordination cooperation between the civilian police and the military police in order to set up joint check-points. I have not seen documents issued or orders issued by General Gotovina on the location of such joint check-points, but it is very important to keep in mind that I've seen shall - and we have discussed some of them - several orders by General Gotovina during and after Operation Storm, indicating that he can use his military police to carry out tasks he has determined.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's start from your proposition now or your answer that you acknowledge that General Lausic issued orders on the establishment of check-points. Major Juric implemented those orders in the field. The issue of check-points, is that a professional line task or an operational task?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It covers both aspects. Because there will be procedures as to how a check-point has to be organised, about -- there will be procedures as to what the general duties or function is of a check-point and where to locate them and so on and so on, than would be -- and we were to locate them in general terms. Like, you're not going to put a check-point in a particular location because of the fact that it wouldn't stop anything, and so on, those aspects would be covered by the professional line. Then the exact physical location of a check-point in location X, Y, or Z, for a particular duration of time, it may be a very specific mission or not, would in my view fall under the operational line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay now let's talk specifics. We're talking 4 August, 5 August, 6 August. We're talking about Major Juric's implementation of check-points in the field his reporting back to General Lausic about where the check-points are, where those check-points have been discontinued. Where those check-points have been moved. Those are operational issues that are being implemented by Major Juric and reported on back to General Lausic, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He reports about it to General Lausic, but I cannot conclude whether -- who orders that a check-point be set up in a particular location at that very moment. I assume or my conclusion is that this follows from the plan that has been agreed between Mr. Lausic -- General Lausic and Mr. Moric, that, okay, the military police will in the framework of its duties to maintain law and order, establish check-points. But from the military practical point of view, there should be and that is a theoretical answer there should be coordination with the operational units or the combat units in the area as to who will set up which check-point where and how they will handle cooperate and coordinate the activities. I cannot be more price because I haven't seen more prices documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I agree with where I think you said your conclusion is that this follows from the plan that had been agreed upon between Mr. Lausic, General Lausic and Mr. Moric. I agree with that conclusion. My -- furthermore would you agree with me that when General Lausic then sends Major Juric into the field, it is with the authority to establish the check-points that he deems necessary in cooperation with the MUP as per the agreement that had been reached on the 3rd of August? I specifically call your attention to the document we referenced earlier which said that Major Juric has the authority to implement all military police tasks in the zone of the 72nd Military Police Battalion.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot draw the conclusion that it the establishment of the check-points, i.e., physically in the terrain at a particular location, fell exclusively under the authority of Major Juric because I haven't seen a document or documents indicating that. And based on my military background, it would be logical - and that's again theoretical - answer that such activities would be coordinated with the operational commander in the area, i.e., the commander of the combat unit in the area, in order to have the most efficient use of all assets available because combat troops, once they have captured the objective, can also be used to establish check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me try it a different way. Based on the fact that we have now established that the issue of these joint check-points was not being reported in terms of their location, their movement, their discontinuance, was not being reported as far as you can tell from the documents that you have reviewed to the Split Military District Command, isn't it -- isn't your conclusion based on the evidence in front you that the fact that this is getting reported up the chain to Juric and Lausic that this must be a task that's being implemented pursuant to that line?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're talking about the joint MUP military police check-points, I think there's a slight distinction with the check-points that are established initially, but, still, as I mentioned in my previous answer, there would have been coordination with the operational commander in the area, in order to ensure that these check-points are located in the most efficient or the most appropriate location and are organised in the most efficient manner, irrespective of who had the initial proposal or idea to set up the check-points. The establishment of these check-points is indeed, based on documents I reviewed, a consequence or a result of the initial plan that is -- has been agreed by general Lausic and Mr. Moric. Now, as to the actual implementation, it would seem plausible that major Juric suggested to the local police official, civilian police official, and, in my view, also the local military commander, that well, we will establish or we want to establish a check-point in location X, Y, or Z, and that is the manner -- according to which the plan is implemented. I cannot imagine that the military police and civilian police would set up their check-points in isolation or disregard of military realities in the area they are without any consultation or cooperation coordination with the operational commander in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Theunens, you have given us an answer about what would you expect, and I keep wanting to get back to what you found. So let me take you back to what you found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, Mr. Theunens apparently combines his military experience and the knowledge he gains from that with what he found in documents, and he has explained to us in different wordings several times that what I see in the documents -- there must be other mechanisms as well. That's what he explained in many different lines. Now, to say, I only want your conclusions on the basis of those documents, if an expert is convinced that on the basis of his experience and his knowledge, that this is most likely incomplete information, the written information, compared to what must have been there to make everything function, that is it not something I would expect you to require from an expert witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, the witness when he is pushed, uses the expression based on my military experience, which to me, I mean, if I were to say to you in closing argument, based on my legal experience, my client is not guilty. You would say, It is an interesting opinion. Is there any evidence to support to you? And I would say, judge, there is all sorts of exculpatory documents based on my experience that have not been shown to you. I'm trying get to conclusions that we can deal with on the basis of what the documents are. And I think that is one conclusion that would be drawn on the basis of documents. The fact that he thinks that it was something else based on his experience in the Belgian army is a different issue can he with address, but I'm primarily interested in, based on the evidence, that this person has been tendered as an expert witness, and I think is he basically testified to that to this point. I don't think it is that controversial to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The expert witness -- if the expert is hesitating to go draw conclusions because on the basis of his experience, he feels that he has not the complete information, that -- of course I can imagine that that would be heavily criticised by you drawing conclusions on incomplete information. I leave that entirely open. But to say I want you to draw conclusions on the basis of documents alone, if the expert feels that, based again on his experience, that he should not do so, then we should respect that. I do not mind at all you've done that over the past one or two hours to very much push him to tell us what the documents tell us. And you have in your questioning clearly explained that if there are vague notions elsewhere, that that should not take -- that he should still should focus on what he investigated. I have no problem with that. But to say, I want you to draw conclusions on the basis of what have you seen, even if that is incomplete, then where the witness has explained various times that he considers there must be more. And of course he has explained it to some extent. He has not just said, there must be more. He has explained that in various respects. I leave it at this point to comments on questions and answers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If I may just respond briefly to say that I think I speak -- I'm sure I speak on behalf of our defence, and I probably speak on behalf of the other two, that we don't accept that hesitation most often results from military experience. I've alluded to certain issues thus far, and I can, I think, establish a pattern of when his hesitation to answer questions appears. And for that reason, I push him because I don't want do give him the opportunity to give me the spin instead of getting to the heart of the matter, and that's why I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, I would not expect you just to accept that the hesitation comes from what the witnesses says. You are there to challenge that. And if you say, We want to push him, that has become perfectly clear. However, pushing to what point? That is the issue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me continue then. Mr. Theunens, these are operational matters, in terms of establishment of check-points. Now, you cannot be sure is the conclusion that you've left at that in terms of who was telling Juric and the members of the military police to establish specific check-points where, although you acknowledge that there is no -- no evidence that you have seen that General Gotovina or the Split Military District Command was issuing orders or receiving reports on where these joint check-points were to be located or were located. My question now goes back to the question that I asked you before the break. If in fact, if in fact, we can logically conclude that Mr. Lausic was there on the 2nd, with the two ministers. He is there at the working meeting on the 3rd with the MUP to work out the details of this plan. He sends out someone from Zagreb, namely, Mr. Juric, into the field with the authority and responsibility to implement all military police tasks in the zone of responsibility. And if, in fact, Major Juric then did, pursuant to his instructions work with the MUP and establish joint check-points at specific locations in the liberated territories, those are operational matters, according to your testimony, in terms of the specific locations. My question to you -- do you disagree with that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I'm just trying to follow your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Those operational matters, and that takes me back to the question before the break. Based on these documents, based on what transpired on th 2nd, 3rd, 4th, is there not a violation of principle of unit of command, if, in fact, Major Juric as someone who is not answerable to the Split Military District Command, is issuing orders on things such as check-points in the field while General Gotovina, in your theory, also has the same ability to issue orders concerning those same check-points?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in light of my previous answer to similar questions, I think I can very clear now. I have not seen specific orders by General Juric to establish a specific check-point in a specific location. On the other hand, I have seen and we have discussed some of those orders by General Gotovina to establish a check-point in a very particular location, whereby a check-point -- excuse me, manned by members of the 72nd Military Police Battalion, whereby General Gotovina or his Deputy Commander, Brigadier Ademi, clearly states what the role of this check-point is. If I had seen such an order by Mr. Juric, I would obviously have drawn a conclusion from those orders. But I haven't seen such orders. I haven't seen any orders indicating where these joint MUP/MP check-points are to be established. All I can say is that there has been indeed been a meeting on the 2nd or 3rd August at the highest level where this procedure or method of ensuring security and safety in the recaptured area is discussed at the highest level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we're coming up on the end of the day, so let me ask it again. I think I know what I'm saying to you is to assume that Mr. Juric based on the sequence of events, in fact, was issuing orders where those check-points go. Take it for granted. It's a hypothetical. Take it for granted. Does that violate the principle of unit of command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the operational commander -- I mean, again hypothetically, if the operational commander in the area agrees that Juric decides on his own or with the MUP, but without consulting the operational commander or coordinating with the operational commander, to establish a check-point in -- in a particular location, there is no problem because the operational commander seems to accept it, even though it does not correspond to with doctrine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if he doesn't accept it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he doesn't accept it, he will raise it with the superior and then through the chain of command --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you're now describing how he would resolve that. The question was now how it would be resolved, but the question was whether it would be a violation of the -- of the one command structure, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, unit of command. There is only violation if somebody -- I mean the operational commander makes a problem of it. If the operational commander accepts it, in theory it is a violation but in practice, it is not. Because the operational commander, if he accepts it, he agrees that he is not consulted in this area and -- so there is there is, in practical terms, no violation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, it's time to adjourn for the day. We'll not sit tomorrow. Mr. Theunens, he'd like to see you back on Friday, at 9.00 in the morning. I give the same instructions to you as I did the other days; that is, not to speak about the testimony, whether already given or still to be given. We adjourn until Friday, the 28th of November, 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 28th day of November, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
